National Cherries Jubilee Day

images.alt:
National Cherries Jubilee Day is an unofficial food holiday celebrated in the United States every year on September 24th. This day honors the classic dessert Cherries Jubilee, which typically consists of cherries and liqueur (often Kirschwasser), flambéed (set aflame) and served as a sauce over vanilla ice cream.
Cherries Jubilee was invented by the famous French chef Auguste Escoffier in the late 19th century. The dessert was originally created to celebrate Queen Victoria's Jubilee (her 50th anniversary as queen), making it a dish with royal roots.
People observe National Cherries Jubilee Day by:
• Making or enjoying Cherries Jubilee at home or in restaurants.
• Sharing recipes and photos on social media.
• Learning about its history and connection to classic flambéed dishes.

World Maritime Day

images.alt:
World Maritime Day is an annual
international observance established by the International Maritime Organization (IMO), a specialized agency of the United Nations. Its main purpose is to highlight the importance of shipping safety, maritime security, the marine environment, and the vital role of the international maritime industry in the world's economy. Usually celebrated on the last Thursday in September each year.
Every year, World Maritime Day focuses on a specific theme chosen by the IMO to reflect current challenges and developments in the maritime sector. Themes have included issues like sustainable shipping, protecting
the marine environment, empowering women in maritime communities, and the digital transformation of the maritime industry. The shipping industry is crucial for global trade, carrying about 80-90% of international goods. 
World Maritime Day aims to:
• Recognize the importance of shipping and seatarers.
• Promote safe, secure, and efficient shipping.
• Raise awareness about the impact of shipping on the environment and efforts to make the industry greener.
• Highlight the contribution of maritime workers to the global economy.
Typical Activities:
• Conferences and seminars
• Educational outreach and media campaigns
• IMO events and official addresses
• Special events in ports and maritime museums

images.alt:
These four are from Dall-E 3. Each depicts a cabin either near or on water, in a forest, as a cyanotype, as per the prompt. 

The first does wonderful things with the trees, causing them to stretch and distort out into a black blob at the top. Vertical striations proliferate around the edges of the image.
This looks like a brush was stroked upward, like in a Bob Ross painting, causing parts of the image to fuzz up. Very noticeable on the roof of the cabin and on the tops of the trees behind.
Warbled effects, like badly distorted vhs tape, distort the trees, most in the upper right of the image. Hints of red, possibly some chromatic aberration, thread through  these distortions.
Mostly upward, fuzzy brush stroke distortions along the tops of trees. The reflections in the water beneath the cabin are also nicely striated.
